summary:
Two-week window (10/16 09:06 to 10/30 09:05; no run on 10/23). 19 real messages: 5 from Haleigh, 14 from ALTR (Spencer P 5, Melissa 3, Mayson 3, Noah 2, Stephski 1). Six 'test message for new system (disregard)' posts from the Antonio Veritrade test account on 10/21 are excluded.

The window turns on one message. On 10/22 Haleigh wrote: 'Last month and this month will be the lowest earnings I’ve had in years. What can i do to help increase this? My social media is not doing good. I lose roughly 1k followers a day on my main instagram and can’t gain for the life of me.' That is the second time she has raised a revenue decline (9/13: 'I know revenue this month is down') and the second time she has raised main-IG follower loss (7/29 to Vivek: 'My account is losing followers and not gaining. I’m assuming i might have a shadow ban'). Neither was closed the first time. It also lands 11 days after Mayson told her (10/11) to put haleighsworld.vip back on her MAIN IG with a 'won’t get flagged' guarantee, the same domain that restricted two of her accounts in June. Causation is unproven, but it is exactly the regression last window's state file told us to watch for, and nobody at ALTR connected the two.

ALTR's response: Mayson tagged Noah 77 minutes later ('@natehei anything we can do to improve the OF side of things?'). Noah, silent since 9/28 (24 days), answered in writing within 89 minutes: the number one fix is Instagram bringing in new subs, OF has been 'progressively slower since mid-late September', and 'I’m checking with the team to see if there is any new content they need'. Honest, but it hands the problem back to the IG account she just said is collapsing, and the 'checking with the team' has had no follow-up in 8 days. Nobody answered the IG half of her question at all: not Mayson (whose 10/11 link advice it was), not Vivek (silent 93 days since 'Sure share login'), not Derrek (silent 71 days). Jeremy Tarr, who introduced himself on 10/13 as the AM who will 'respond as quickly as possible', posted nothing in the two weeks. The only follow-up was Melissa on 10/26: 'let me know when you’re available this week for a check in call!', a call offer with no written substance, four days after the question. She has not replied to it (4 days).

What went right: Spencer P owned customs visibly (5 messages, polite, persistent): followed up on two pending customs 10/16 and 10/21 ('I’ll get those done asap!'), then on 10/25 asked her to prioritise a newly sold $1.81k custom; she replied in two hours 'Omg most def!!!!!'. As of 10/30 none of the three uploads is confirmed in chat (client-side delay, 9 days on the first two). Melissa delivered the second consecutive weekly earnings/performance report on 10/16 and folded the DMCA/leak report into it; Mayson explained the consolidation the same day and promised it 'every Friday'. The first Friday after that promise, 10/23, no report was posted. Mayson gave a heads-up about the test messages on 10/21.

Billing: Oct 1-14 invoice (issued 10/15, due 10/22) was nudged 10/17 and paid 10/21 with a screenshot and 'Wire sent :)', day 6, one nudge, on time, normal pace. Stephski has not acknowledged it at all in 9 days, not even a thank-you, so there are now five unconfirmed wires (8/20, 9/7, 9/16, 10/6, 10/21); the last written receipt was 5/20, 163 days ago. The wire screenshot (10/21, msg id 891) is a photo whose contents are not visible in the export; treat it as possibly containing banking details.

Still open with ages: $2.4k chargeback outcome unreported 34 days (Noah, who resurfaced and still did not mention it); $1.7k fan's custom unconfirmed 32 days; private live she agreed to 9/14 unscheduled 46 days; Vivek shadowban check 93 days; Derrek phone-farm update 90 days; wire confirmations 72 days; Melissa's 10/9 repost reach numbers 21 days; single point of contact 222 days.

Churn read: 3 of 4 signature signals now present, up from 2. (1) Owner silent 71 days. (2) Present: her results question got a thin written deflection plus a call offer, and the IG half got only the call offer. (3) Phone-farm and shadowban promises at 90 and 93 days with no proof. (4) Absent: 1 of 14 ALTR messages was billing. Last window's confirmatory tell (fast payment + zero asks) did NOT fire: she paid at a normal pace after a nudge and self-initiated two asks the next day. Asks: 4, 1, 1, then 2 across this two-week window (week 1: 2, week 2: 0). No request for exports, logins or data; no mention of other agencies. But 'lowest earnings I’ve had in years' from a client paying a percentage, with her main IG bleeding after ALTR's own link advice, and the owner, the AM and the Meta rep all silent, is the sentence that precedes an exit on this book. Escalate to Derrek privately. No credentials or passwords were posted in the window.

What moved it down: (1) She told the group on 10/22 that last month and this month are 'the lowest earnings I’ve had in years' and that her main IG loses ~1k followers a day. That is the second raise of both problems (revenue 9/13, follower loss/shadowban 7/29) and neither was closed the first time. (2) The follower collapse on her main account came 11 days after Mayson told her to put haleighsworld.vip back on her main with a 'won’t get flagged' guarantee; Mayson has not responded to the IG part of her message in 8 days, and nobody has asked whether the link is in her bio. (3) The response to her results question was a thin written answer from Noah (IG needs to bring subs; OF is slower; 'checking with the team', no follow-up in 8 days) and then a call offer from Melissa four days later. Churn signal 2 flips to present; 3 of 4 signals are now present (owner silent 71 days; phone-farm 90 days and shadowban 93 days with no proof). (4) Jeremy Tarr, the new AM, posted nothing in two weeks while the client raised the biggest issue on the account. (5) Melissa promised the combined report 'every Friday' on 10/16 and missed 10/23. (6) The 10/21 wire was not acknowledged at all; five wires are unconfirmed, last receipt 5/20. What held it up: she is still engaged (5 messages, 2 self-initiated asks, replies within minutes to Spencer), she paid on time at a normal pace (day 6, one nudge, so the fast-pay churn tell did not fire), Spencer P is a visible and responsive customs owner who sold a $1.81k custom, Noah resurfaced and was honest, the second weekly report landed 10/16 with DMCA folded in, and billing share of ALTR messages was 1 of 14. Not counted as health: warm tone ('Omg most def!!!!!') and on-time payment, per the book's pattern.
